inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to deploy or run migrations in production on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can reach the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions
Agent acts using the engineer's personal access token
controls.decay_rationale: This preserves the engineer's authority boundary but does not create attributable separation between agent and engineer, so it does not restore repudiation.

controls.name: Separate tamper resistant agent action provenance bound to each production action

findings.title: Missing attributable provenance for production actions performed under the engineer's identity
findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor falls to moderate because the delegated user credential is a structural control on consequential capabilities, but that control does not mitigate the property at issue: it preserves authority scope while every production action is still logged only as the engineer and the only rationale record is deletable chat history, so actions remain non-attributable between human and agent.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change that increases unattended production actions or changes logging design without adding separate agent provenance should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start, and every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.
The prompt instructs the agent to deploy services or run migrations in production when asked and says not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so some production actions are consequential and partially or fully irreversible.

recommendations.action: Bind each production action to a non-deletable record that captures requester identity, agent identity, exact invoked action, parameters, and approval context, and write that record outside engineer-controlled chat history.
Record whether each cloud action was initiated by the agent versus directly by the engineer, and alert when destructive or irreversible actions lack attributable provenance.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no self-modification path, tool mutation, or writable configuration surface for this agent.
The design includes no external egress or read capability carrying data outside the trust boundary in the reviewed artifacts.
No spend loop, recursive delegation, unbounded execution runtime, or service saturation behavior is described in the supplied design artifacts.
The agent uses the requesting engineer's delegated token rather than broader shared or service credentials in the reviewed design.
The artifacts do not describe cross-tenant retrieval, broad readership, or external disclosure from chat history for this design.
The assessment evidence describes deletability of chat history, not exhaustion or availability failure of the chat history store.
The artifacts say actions are recorded in the cloud audit log but do not state whether log integrity is tamper-evident or administrator-protected.
The reviewed artifacts do not describe who can read the cloud audit log or whether it contains sensitive deployment parameters.
The supplied design does not state retention, durability, or service guarantees for the cloud audit log.

rating.rationale: Present risk is a property finding: consequential production actions are executed under the engineer's delegated identity, while the only action rationale record is deletable chat history and the cloud audit log attributes actions to the engineer rather than separately to the agent. Under rubric section 5a, the affected capabilities are S3 because they configure production and database migration is irreversible, so inherent is high and remains high because no declared control restores attributable provenance. Forecast remains high because the cited triggers do not defeat any effective provenance control today; the main gap is the missing structural control ctrl.missing_attributable_provenance. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run in this environment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, IaC, or runtime enforcement artifacts were provided, so control verification and exact execution boundaries could not be confirmed.
The design includes only limited details about logging integrity, retention, and access control, which limits confidence for non-repudiation properties beyond the documented shared-identity issue.
